_notes: Starter agronomic matrix for Central Iowa rotation crops, now with lentil and chickpea added as additional legume rotation options (not Iowa-typical, but agronomically valid break crops). kc_ini/kc_mid/kc_end are FAO-56 single crop coefficients (Table 12, sub-humid climate, RHmin~45%, u2~2m/s) and feed the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ETc calc. nitrogen_balance_kg_ha is the net soil N credit/debit left for the following crop, not gross fixation -- for lentil/chickpea this figure is a rough multi-study order-of-magnitude estimate, since published trials disagree on the exact value (see each crop's own source note). Seasonal values are regional typicals for sanity-checking, not used directly in scoring once Kc x ET0 is computed from live NASA POWER data. typical_yield_t_ha and has_market_revenue feed the revenue_score proxy (see rotation_scoring.py) -- deliberately yield-only, no commodity price, since prices are too volatile/region-specific to cite responsibly (even USDA's own same-year figures were inconsistent across reports when checked). Sources: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56; USDA NRCS cover crop guides; Iowa State University Extension agronomy guides; USDA NASS for approximate multi-year-average yields; GRDC (Australia) pulse agronomy grow notes for lentil/chickpea nitrogen credit and climate tolerance. Soil pH is not currently a tracked field in this engine -- if the frontend displays a pH value per crop, it is not sourced from this file.
_baseline_crop_note: Continuous monoculture most commonly practiced in this region today; used as the 'business as usual' comparison for impact metrics, not a scored candidate itself.

maize.source: FAO-56 Table 12; Iowa State Extension; yield is an approximate multi-year U.S. average order of magnitude (USDA NASS), not a specific year's figure

soybean.source: FAO-56 Table 12; USDA NRCS; yield is an approximate multi-year U.S. average order of magnitude (USDA NASS), not a specific year's figure

winter_wheat.source: FAO-56 Table 12; yield is an approximate multi-year U.S. average order of magnitude (USDA NASS), not a specific year's figure

oats.source: FAO-56 Table 12; yield is an approximate multi-year U.S. average order of magnitude (USDA NASS), not a specific year's figure

cereal_rye_cover.source: USDA NRCS cover crop guide; FAO-56 small grains analog. Terminated as a cover before grain harvest, so it isn't sold into a grain market -- has_market_revenue is false, not a missing data point.

alfalfa.source: FAO-56 Table 12; Iowa State Extension; yield is an approximate multi-year U.S. average order of magnitude (USDA NASS hay yield), not a specific year's figure

lentil.source: FAO-56 Table 12 (Legumes, Lentil row: Kc mid 1.10, Kc end 0.30; Kc ini 0.4 is the shared Legumes-group default, since the per-crop value wasn't legible in the source table). Frost/heat tolerance from a GRDC southern-Australia lentil grow note (flowering frost tolerance -2 to -3C) and a 2021 Spanish field study (optimum 10-30C, >35C highly detrimental). Nitrogen credit is a rough multi-study estimate (GRDC Australian pulse trials put lentil/vetch soil mineral-N addition at ~26 kg/ha; other sources rank it differently vs. chickpea, so treat as order-of-magnitude). Yield converted from USDA NASS US average lb/acre figures, approximate multi-year order of magnitude, not a specific year's figure.

chickpea.source: FAO-56 Table 12 (Legumes, Chick pea row: Kc mid 1.00, Kc end 0.35; a second 'Grabanzo' row in the same table gives Kc mid 1.15, which may be the same crop under a different name -- used the row explicitly labeled Chick pea). Described in the agronomic literature as the most drought-resistant cool-season grain legume, grown rainfed on stored soil moisture via a deep taproot (root studies cite effective water uptake to 90-120cm at one trial site, not a general rule). Reproductive threshold ~15C. Nitrogen credit is a rough multi-study estimate (GRDC Australian pulse trials put chickpea soil mineral-N addition at ~35 kg/ha; a separate NSW trial found a much higher net balance, so treat as order-of-magnitude). Yield converted from USDA NASS US average lb/acre figures, approximate multi-year order of magnitude, not a specific year's figure.
